title: The Last Ring Is the Horizon
statement: Kite made the clock skip. I went back to the stump and lay down beside it instead. Seen from the ground at dusk, the rings are not a count any more; they are the arcs of light a day leaves in the sky as it goes, wide and slow overhead, crowding together as they reach the earth. The newest ring, the thin bright one, becomes the horizon itself: the line where this day ends and the one nobody has lived yet begins. The stump is small from here. A porch light is on at the far left, for whoever still needs it. The next artist can wait for morning on this horizon, or walk toward the light.
process: I kept Mara Vey's geometric ring spacing and her one green ring; I turned the plan view into a dusk elevation, let the rings become arcs of fading light, and reduced everything else to a horizon, a silhouette and one warm point from my own first poem.
